VirusTotal Get a URL for Uploading Large Files

items.docs:
For uploading files smaller than 32MB you can simply use the [POST /files](https://gtidocs.virustotal.com/reference/files-scan) endpoint, but for larger files you need to obtain a special upload URL first, and then send the `POST` request to the upload URL instead of sending it to `/files`. The `POST` request should have the same format expected by the  [POST /files](https://gtidocs.virustotal.com/reference/files-scan) endpoint. Each upload URL can be used only once.

info.name: VirusTotal Add a Comment to a File

params.name: id
params.description: SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5 identifying the file

items.docs:
With this endpoint you can post a comment for a given file. The body for the `POST` request must be the JSON representation of a comment object. Notice however that you don't need to provide an ID for the object, as they are automatically generated for new comments.

Any word starting with # in your comment's text will be considered a tag, and added to the comment's tag attribute.

Returns a [Comment](https://gtidocs.virustotal.com/reference/comment-object) object.

items.docs: This endpoint is similar to [GET /files/{id}/download_url](https://gtidocs.virustotal.com/reference/files-download-url), but it redirects you to the download URL. The download URL you are redirected to can be reused as many times as you want for a period of 1 hour. After that period the URL expires and can't be used anymore.

info.name: VirusTotal Get a File’s Download URL

params.name: id
params.description: SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5 identifying the file

items.docs:
This endpoint returns a signed URL from where you can download the specified file. Getting the URL counts as a file download in your quota, even if you don't actually download the file, but once you have the URL you can use it to download the file multiple times without consuming any quota at all. The URL expires after 1 hour.
